tools.name: inspect_firmware_regions
tools.title: Inspect Firmware Regions
tools.description: Inspect signature candidates in a local firmware file with Binwalk 3.1.x (verified with 3.1.0). Returns offsets, reported lengths, descriptions and raw confidence values. Length validation and runtime addresses remain unknown. No extraction or target execution. Linux, caller-supplied tool, util-linux prlimit and procps ps required; 128 MiB input limit, one worker. Adjust analysis_timeout_ms for the analysis wall-clock budget (default 120000); fixed per-process limits are unchanged.

tools.name: extract_firmware
tools.title: Extract Firmware
tools.description: Extract selected local firmware bytes with Unblob 26.6.x (verified with 26.6.4) into an absent output directory. Returns verified child paths/digests, derivations, uncovered ranges, unknown chunks and extraction_gaps with continuation_id recovery instructions. Linux, format-specific extractors, prlimit and procps ps are required. Preserves the sandbox and publishes only regular files; no mounts or extracted-code execution. Select a returned native file with open_binary for analysis. Decompressed offsets are not original-file addresses.

tools.name: inspect_uefi_firmware
tools.title: Inspect Uefi Firmware
tools.description: Map PI firmware volumes, FFS files, section chains, AMD PSP directory candidates and uncovered ranges in a local flash image. Report integrity observations and coverage limits. LZMA-custom, LZMAF86, and AMD-zlib streams can contain nested volumes or section chains. Decoded offsets are relative to the stream identified by source_stream. EFI standard compression and other unsupported handlers remain explicit limitations.

tools.name: extract_uefi_firmware
tools.title: Extract Uefi Firmware
tools.description: Extract FFS bodies and section payloads from a local UEFI image into an absent directory. A volume, file or section selection includes its descendants. Use source_stream with an offset from a decoded stream or when offsets are ambiguous. Results include SHA-256, source ranges and decode derivations; original_file_range is null for decoded bytes. Unsupported carriers are optional and decoding gaps remain visible. Pass an extracted PE32 file to open_binary for executable analysis.

tools.name: inspect_uefi_nvram
tools.title: Inspect Uefi Nvram
tools.description: Map valid AMI NVAR entries inside a local flash image, including nested factory defaults such as StdDefaults. Reports raw link displacements, attributes, inline GUIDs or GUID-table indices, data ranges and SHA-256 digests. Data-only records have no name or GUID reference. Links describe the image bytes. The parser walks physical records and reports the nesting depth and parent offset. No external tools or target execution are required.

tools.name: inspect_android_jni_bindings
tools.title: Inspect Android Jni Bindings
tools.description: Link an APK's DEX native declarations to Java_* exports and static JNINativeMethod candidates by ABI and exact library occurrence, without executing it or loading libraries. Returns digests, relation IDs, slot/relocation provenance and explicit partial/unknown coverage; a candidate match does not prove uniqueness or runtime registration. Optional view kind android-jni selects bindings/declarations/candidates/libraries, fields and pages; use inspect_analysis_view with parent_evidence_id for later pages. Empty selections match none. Requires caller-supplied JADX MCP JAR and JDK.

tools.name: inspect_android_package
tools.title: Inspect Android Package
tools.description: Inspect APK package/SDK/permission declarations, decoded manifest, static components and class/resource counts without executing it or verifying signatures. Requires caller-supplied JADX MCP JAR and JDK. Default complete returns full Evidence; detail summary retains it and omits manifest text/raw duplicates. With summary, view kind android selects facet components (exact filters, fields, paging), component-summary or manifest (UTF-16 text pages); complete detail rejects view. Use normalized_result.parent_evidence_id with inspect_analysis_view for later views. Component source_index identifies the original declaration, and declaration_coverage marks partial declarations.

tools.name: search_android_classes
tools.title: Search Android Classes
tools.description: Search complete top-level decompiler class-name rows in an explicit local APK by case-sensitive substring. Empty query inventories all rows. Repeated names remain repeated and appear in duplicate_names; the provider accepts only class names for lookup, so these rows do not identify which same-name class node a later lookup selects. Retains artifact and engine identity; no APK execution.

tools.name: inspect_android_class
tools.title: Inspect Android Class
tools.description: Inspect one exact Android class's methods, fields, inner classes, DEX prototypes and encoded static final values without generating source. Select an overload_index from these results for inspect_android_method; indices are artifact/engine-session scoped and prototypes are not complete raw method IDs. Optional mapping_path adds verified R8/ProGuard names separately; observed names remain primary. detail summary retains complete Evidence and returns normalized symbols without duplicate raw calls; complete remains the default.

tools.name: inspect_android_method
tools.title: Inspect Android Method

Reports DEX prototype, representation, fallback markers and source truncation; display signatures may be aliases. Optional mapping_path annotates R8/ProGuard names without replacing observed names. detail summary retains complete Evidence and returns the selected body without duplicate class metadata; complete remains the default. Use inspect_android_class to choose the overload.

tools.name: trace_android_references
tools.title: Trace Android References

No reflection, JNI or runtime dispatch is inferred.

tools.name: inspect_pcap_client

tools.name: inspect_pcap_capture
tools.title: Inspect Pcap Capture

Use inspect_packet_capture for caller-selected TShark fields or display filters. Default complete returns full Evidence; detail summary retains it for inspect_analysis_view kind pcap. tools.name: identify_flutter_build

Complete snapshot coverage currently expects two independent headers in the legacy split VM/isolate profile; unified and other layouts can yield partial build facts. The snapshot hash maps to a Dart SDK release through an external dataset; REA performs no lookup. No engine, no execution, no external tools.

tools.name: inspect_dart_aot
tools.title: Inspect Dart Aot
tools.description: Inspect one APK ABI's Dart AOT snapshot without executing it. Supports legacy split VM/isolate FullAOT kind 3 and unified FullAOT kind 2. Returns the observed profile, snapshot exports, headers, hashes and bounded package:/dart:/identifier-like byte-pattern strings. pool_policy.contains selects strings before collection; other pool budgets do not raise APK/ELF/response limits. Default complete returns all facts; detail summary retains them for inspect_analysis_view kind dart-aot, collections package_uris/dart_uris/class_like_tokens, using parent_evidence_id and row paging. Counts are lower bounds and page exhaustion never proves complete pool coverage.

tools.name: list_frida_devices
tools.title: List Frida Devices
tools.description: List Frida devices currently available to this host, optionally connecting to the caller-selected remote Frida endpoint. Remote authentication options are used for this call only and are never returned or recorded.

tools.name: list_frida_processes
tools.title: List Frida Processes
tools.description:
List processes observed on a selected Frida device or caller-supplied remote endpoint. A remote connection is closed after discovery; authentication values are never returned or recorded.

tools.name: start_frida_session
tools.title: Start Frida Session
tools.description: Attach Frida to one selected process or spawn one selected target. Spawned targets remain paused until resume_frida_session, allowing scripts to load before execution. Closing a session detaches instrumentation; it does not kill the target.

tools.name: load_frida_script
tools.title: Load Frida Script
tools.description: Load caller-supplied JavaScript into a Frida session. Scripts can read or change target memory and behavior and can access the target process's capabilities. Messages and script errors are returned inline as Evidence; source content is not persisted.

tools.name: resume_frida_session
tools.title: Resume Frida Session

tools.name: unload_frida_script
tools.title: Unload Frida Script
tools.description: Unload one caller-selected Frida script from a live session. This removes that script's instrumentation from the target.

tools.name: frida_session_status
tools.title: Frida Session Status
tools.description: Read observed Frida session state on each call. Default detail=complete returns queued script messages and capture truncation. detail=summary retains the complete observation in this session and returns identity, state, scripts, retained message count and truncation without payloads. Export the complete parent with export_evidence_bundle; retained summaries are historical and never refresh live state.

tools.name: close_frida_session
tools.title: Close Frida Session
tools.description: Unload session scripts and attempt to detach REA's Frida session. Then resume a still-paused spawned process if script cleanup or session detach confirms instrumentation was released. Cleanup failures are reported. REA never kills the target; its final state is reported as unknown.

tools.name: instrument_with_frida
tools.title: Instrument With Frida
tools.description: Run caller-authored Frida JavaScript against a selected process for one observation window, then detach. Scripts can read/change target memory and behavior and use the process's capabilities. CLI and MCP share this ephemeral workflow; use start_frida_session/load_frida_script for a persistent session. Remote authentication is call-local and excluded from Evidence. Detachment does not establish target termination.

tools.name: inspect_apktool_client
tools.title: Inspect Apktool Client
tools.description: Inspect the caller-selected apktool launcher: resolved command, selection source, and version. Decodes nothing. REA never installs Apktool or Java; select a launcher with REA_APKTOOL_COMMAND (absolute) or apktool on PATH.

tools.name: decode_android_resources
tools.title: Decode Android Resources
tools.description: Decode APK resources with apktool d --no-src: readable manifest, version/SDK facts, string resources/locales and decoded file count. Uses a temporary workspace removed after projection; smali/source recovery belongs to JADX. tools.name: inspect_jeb_client
tools.title: Inspect Jeb Client

tools.name: list_jeb_units
tools.title: List Jeb Units

tools.name: decompile_jeb_item
tools.title: Decompile Jeb Item

Read-only with respect to the target file.

tools.name: inspect_adb_client
tools.title: Inspect Adb Client
tools.description: Inspect the caller-selected adb client: resolved binary, version, and install path. Never contacts devices and never starts the adb server. REA never installs platform tools; select a binary with REA_ADB_PATH (absolute) or adb on PATH.

tools.name: list_adb_devices
tools.title: List Adb Devices
tools.description: List attached devices exactly as `adb devices -l` reports them: serial, state, transport, model metadata, and an inferred emulator/physical kind with its evidence basis. May start the local adb server on first use.

tools.name: inspect_adb_device
tools.title: Inspect Adb Device
tools.description: Inspect one device's build identity through a fixed `getprop` whitelist: Android and SDK versions, security patch, fingerprint, product identity, CPU ABIs, and debuggable flag, plus the observed emulator indicator ro.kernel.qemu. Present properties retain empty values; omitted keys were not reported. Read-only with respect to the device.

tools.name: list_adb_packages
tools.title: List Adb Packages
tools.description: List installed packages on one device with each base APK's device path, optionally scoped to third-party or system packages. Paths are device filesystem paths, not host-local. Read-only.

tools.name: pull_adb_package
tools.title: Pull Adb Package
tools.description: Pull one installed package's complete APK set (base plus every split, as `pm path` reports) from the device into a caller-selected output directory, creating a package-named subdirectory that must not already exist. Every pulled file is digested with SHA-256; partial pulls keep successful artifacts and per-file failure reasons. The device keeps the originals.

tools.name: read_adb_logcat
tools.title: Read Adb Logcat
tools.description: Read a bounded dump of the device log (`logcat -d -t`) for one buffer, optionally restricted to a process id. No streaming, no clearing; the newest lines are kept when the count cap trims. Read-only.

tools.name: inspect_adb_package
tools.title: Inspect Adb Package
tools.description: Inspect installed-package versions, install times, installer, user id, flags, and requested-permission count through read-only `dumpsys package`. Malformed numeric declarations are retained in bounded numeric_issues and make coverage partial; version_code stays exact text. Unknown sections are not inferred.

tools.name: pull_adb_file
tools.title: Pull Adb File
tools.description: Pull one absolute device path (a database, shared-preferences XML, or any readable file) into a caller-selected output directory, digesting it with SHA-256. The local copy must not already exist. Read-only with respect to the device.

tools.name: push_adb_file
tools.title: Push Adb File
tools.description: Push one local file to an absolute device path. If the destination is an existing directory, adb places the file inside it under the local basename and the result reports that file path. A device-mutating tool: checks for an existing destination file before transfer and refuses it unless overwrite is explicitly requested; this check is not atomic and another process can create the path before adb writes. The private staged copy remains non-writable and preserves source executable bits. When the device provides sha256sum, the transfer is verified by comparing it with the local digest.

tools.name: capture_adb_screen
tools.title: Capture Adb Screen
tools.description: Capture one frame of the device screen as a PNG (`screencap -p` through exec-out, no device-side file) into a caller-selected output directory, digesting it and reporting its dimensions. No recording or interaction.

tools.name: list_adb_processes
tools.title: List Adb Processes
tools.description: List running processes exactly as `ps -A` reports them: user, pid, ppid, rss, state, and name. Useful for pairing with instrumentation lanes. Read-only.

tools.name: list_adb_directory
tools.title: List Adb Directory
tools.description: List the immediate children of one absolute device directory, including hidden entries: names, kinds, permissions, owner, group, sizes, dates, and symlink targets. Names and targets preserve embedded newlines. Recognizes the standard errors for absent paths and denied reads. Read-only.

tools.name: list_adb_features
tools.title: List Adb Features
tools.description: List the device's declared hardware and software features (`pm list features`) for device fingerprinting. Read-only.

tools.name: list_adb_services
tools.title: List Adb Services
tools.description: List the device's binder services with their interfaces (`service list`). Read-only.

tools.name: inspect_adb_display
tools.title: Inspect Adb Display
tools.description: Read physical and override size/density from `wm size` and `wm density`. Malformed numeric declarations are retained in numeric_issues with partial coverage; optional values remain null. Required physical-size failures retain partial display facts. Read-only.

tools.name: inspect_adb_window
tools.title: Inspect Adb Window
tools.description: Report the window manager's focus declarations with display context, original lines and explicit summary status. Reads `dumpsys window windows`, falling back to `displays` only when no focus field is declared. Singular fields are unknown for multiple contexts or repeated declarations; inspect focus_contexts for every observation. Read-only; no interaction occurs.

tools.name: read_adb_setting
tools.title: Read Adb Setting
tools.description: Read one settings value (`settings get`) from the system, secure, or global namespace. Absent keys report the device's own null observation. Read-only; writing settings is not exposed.

tools.name: collect_adb_bugreport
tools.title: Collect Adb Bugreport
tools.description: Collect one device-generated bugreport archive (`adb bugreport`) into a caller-selected output directory, digesting the zip. The archive contains the device's own dumpstate, dumpsys, and logcat report; collection can take minutes. Read-only with respect to configuration.

tools.name: resolve_adb_packages
tools.title: Resolve Adb Packages
tools.description: Find installed packages by case-insensitive package-name substring and return each base APK device path. Pass an exact returned name to pull_adb_package to retrieve its base and split APKs. Read-only.

tools.name: install_adb_package
tools.title: Install Adb Package
tools.description: Install one local APK on the device (`adb install [-r]`), recording the APK's host digest and byte size. A device-mutating tool: `replace_requested` records whether `-r` was selected; `replaced` is null because install success does not establish prior package state. The device's own Success/Failure verdict is preserved with its reason.

tools.name: uninstall_adb_package
tools.title: Uninstall Adb Package
tools.description: Request package removal for user 0 (`adb shell pm uninstall --user 0`) without data retention. A device-mutating tool; absent packages report the device's own refusal reason.

tools.name: start_adb_app
tools.title: Start Adb App
tools.description: Start one installed app's resolved launcher activity with `am start -W -n`. A device-mutating tool for dynamic analysis. The full wait report determines success; failures retain launch-attempt facts and raw output. Pair with `read_adb_logcat` (pid filter) and `list_adb_processes` to observe the app, and `stop_adb_app` to end the run.

tools.name: start_adb_activity
tools.title: Start Adb Activity
tools.description: Start an intent with `am start -W`: one action, optional data URI, optional explicit component, and up to 16 typed extras (string, boolean, int, long, float). A device-mutating tool; the full wait report determines success, with failed-attempt facts and raw output retained.

tools.name: stop_adb_app
tools.title: Stop Adb App
tools.description: Force-stop every process of one package (`am force-stop`), ending a dynamic-analysis run. A device-mutating tool; it succeeds whether or not the package had running processes.

tools.name: list_browser_targets
tools.title: List Browser Targets
tools.description: List pages exposed by one loopback Chrome DevTools Protocol endpoint, optionally filtered by exact origin. Returns target IDs and URLs; query values and fragments are preserved, with URL userinfo credentials removed. Use a returned target ID with inspect_web_page. discovery_timeout_ms controls discovery; command_timeout_ms does not apply. Browser-socket endpoints remain shared by the active browser provider until it closes or target-session cleanup is unconfirmed; cancellation/deadline on a clean socket releases only this call’s lease.

tools.name: inspect_web_page
tools.title: Inspect Web Page
tools.description:
Passively inspect one selected page target through CDP without evaluating JavaScript, navigating, clicking, closing, or mutating the page. If no origin filter is supplied, capture is scoped to the target's current origin. Returns DOM structure, accessibility, scripts, resources, attach-window network and console metadata, workers, and redacted storage inventory as Evidence.

Provide a complete input group: cdp_endpoint + target_id + [allowed_origins] + [discovery_timeout_ms] + [command_timeout_ms] + [observation_ms] + [include_accessibility_text] + [include_console_text] + [include_json_body_shapes] + [include_websocket_shapes] + [include_storage_keys] + [include_storage_fingerprints] + [include_script_sources]; cdp_endpoint + target_id + include_script_sources + [allowed_origins] + [discovery_timeout_ms] + [command_timeout_ms] + [observation_ms] + [include_accessibility_text] + [include_console_text] + [include_json_body_shapes] + [include_websocket_shapes] + [include_storage_keys] + [include_storage_fingerprints].

tools.name: analyze_web_bundle
tools.title: Analyze Web Bundle
tools.description:
Recover a static chunk graph, route/endpoint candidates, vendor fingerprints and page-declared WebMCP metadata from JavaScript on one selected CDP page. May fetch source maps only from the target origin or explicitly selected origins; application JavaScript is not executed. detail summary retains complete Evidence; view {kind: "web-bundle", collection: "endpoints"} selects endpoint rows, and javascript-routes views select route patterns/occurrences/sources/unknowns. Read later pages with inspect_analysis_view. Static candidates do not establish runtime reachability or a complete route set.

Advertised in reduced form by the compact input schema profile; the server still validates complete canonical inputs.

cdp_endpoint.description: Literal loopback CDP endpoint: http://127.0.0.1:PORT, or ws://127.0.0.1:PORT/devtools/browser/ID.

discovery_timeout_ms.description: Loopback CDP HTTP discovery per-response deadline and browser-socket handshake plus discovery (Browser.getVersion, Target.getTargets) deadline in milliseconds (default 10000). Omitted means 10000 and applies on the next call. Separate from command_timeout_ms, the caller observation window, and the 5000 ms cleanup grace. Does not raise the fixed HTTP discovery document or WebSocket protocol byte budgets, which have no runtime override.

target_id.description: Exact CDP target identifier selected from the endpoint's target listing.

command_timeout_ms.description: CDP WebSocket handshake and per-command response deadline in milliseconds (default 20000). Omitted means 20000 and applies on the next call. deadlineExpired for a handshake or command is not the caller observation window, not the CDP discovery deadline (default 10000 ms, or discovery_timeout_ms where supported), and not the 5000 ms cleanup grace. It also bounds passive script-source collection and the inspection/source-join phase that share this deadline. Does not raise the fixed protocol, retained-event, or source byte budgets, or the cleanup grace, which have no runtime override.

include_accessibility_text.description: Whether to include accessibility text in the result.

include_console_text.description: Whether to include console text in the result.

include_json_body_shapes.description: Whether to include json body shapes in the result.

include_websocket_shapes.description: Whether to include websocket shapes in the result.

include_storage_keys.description: Whether to include storage keys in the result.

include_storage_fingerprints.description: Whether to include storage fingerprints in the result.

include_script_sources.description: Whether to include script sources in the result.

semantic_precision.description: Per-script semantic evaluator budgets; omitted fields preserve defaults. Independent of worker memory, deadlines and reply budgets.

source_map_limits.description: Source-map fetch/representation and decoder admission for this call. Omitted fields keep existing defaults; no restart required.

max_heap_mb.description: Heap phase: maximum V8 old-space for the isolated inert-script analyzer, in MiB (default 1024, range 128..16384). Omitted means 1024 and applies on the next call. This is not a total process RSS limit, not analysis_timeout_ms, and not total_analysis_timeout_ms. Bun ignores V8 flags; Windows Bun uses an owned process commit limit plus a 512 MiB runtime reserve, while other Bun hosts have no enforced memory limit. Raising max_heap_mb does not raise the fixed worker protocol or result byte budgets.

analysis_timeout_ms.description: Per-script deadline phase: maximum startup, analysis and result transfer time for one captured script, in milliseconds (default 30000, range 1..2147483647). Omitted means 30000. deadlineExpired for one script is not total_analysis_timeout_ms. A per-script value above the effective total is rejected. Timed-out scripts are explicit unknowns and other scripts may still be analyzed. Applies on the next call.

total_analysis_timeout_ms.description: Total analysis deadline phase: maximum time for all captured-script analysis, in milliseconds (default 300000, range 1..2147483647). Omitted means 300000. This is not the per-script analysis_timeout_ms, not capture, and not source-map fetch. A per-script timeout above this total is rejected. Unstarted scripts remain explicit unknowns. Applies on the next call.

source_map_fetch_timeout_ms.description: Source-map fetch deadline in milliseconds (default 30000). Omitted means 30000 and applies on the next fetch. After response cleanup completes, a fetch overrun is an item limitation (fetch_failed), not a thrown analysis timeout. Pending or failed response cleanup is reported as an error with its retained owner. Response/representation and decoder budgets are independent source_map_limits fields.

tools.name: observe_web_session
tools.title: Observe Web Session
tools.description: Arm a CDP observation window of the requested duration while the user operates the page. By default it follows the selected target's current origin; an explicit origin list controls which origins may be retained. Records navigation, redirect, lifecycle, and failure events.

tools.name: discover_webmcp_tools
tools.title: Discover Webmcp Tools
tools.description: Passively inventory every page-registered WebMCP tool and its complete structural input-schema summary using the experimental CDP WebMCP domain. Metadata is page-declared-untrusted; REA never registers or invokes discovered tools.

tools.name: compare_web_captures
tools.title: Compare Web Captures
tools.description:
Compare two passive page inspections or two recorded browser scenarios. For passive captures, pass before/after with each complete inspect_web_page normalized_result in inspection and optional complete discover_webmcp_tools normalized_result in webmcp. For scenarios, pass complete normalized_result objects as before_scenario/after_scenario; use exactly one input group. Returns artifact differences and alignment failures. Scenario steps align by exact IDs; optional literal normalization is recorded. HTTP requests and ordered WebSocket streams are compared without inventing stable identities for same-URL connections. Missing or truncated Evidence never proves equality.

Provide a complete input group: before + after; before_scenario + after_scenario + [normalization].

tools.name: capture_web_screenshot
tools.title: Capture Web Screenshot
tools.description: Capture the current visible viewport of one configured page as an inline, content-addressed PNG artifact. The operation never scrolls, navigates, or evaluates page JavaScript.

tools.name: compare_web_screenshots
tools.title: Compare Web Screenshots
tools.description: Compare two self-verifying PNG screenshot artifacts with local pixel metrics. Returns exact changed-pixel ratios and channel deltas without OCR or external services.

tools.name: capture_browser_scenario
tools.title: Capture Browser Scenario
tools.description:
Drive a browser scenario when passive observation cannot exercise the app. Launch the selected executable or connect to a loopback CDP target; actions can change application state and make network requests. Supply browser, start_url and actions, e.g. {browser:{mode:"launch",executable_path:"/opt/chromium/chrome"},start_url:{url:"https://app.example.test/"},actions:[{step_id:"settle",action:"wait_for_timeout",duration_ms:250}]}. Empty storage and a URL-only final capture are defaults. Request actions use page fetch on the start origin; capture.network independently opts into request_body, response_body and header_values. Credentials and declared secrets are redacted. capture.limits controls retained event/content budgets; omissions identify affected events/transactions. Role locators match the exact full accessible name. Actions wait for completion or cancellation; per-action timeout_ms bounds a step. Default complete delivery returns Evidence inline. detail summary retains it and returns step outcomes, final/first-unsuccessful accessibility, and counts; inspect_analysis_view kind browser-scenario pages steps, events, transactions and UTF-16 text. Use inspect_web_page for observation without actions.

Advertised in reduced form by the compact input schema profile; the server still validates complete canonical inputs.

browser.description: Required launch/connect selection. Launch uses the selected executable and an owned temporary profile; connect uses one loopback CDP endpoint and target.

start_url.description: Required initial HTTP(S) URL. Query values must be declared separately as public literals or secret references.

environment.description: Optional deterministic browser settings. Defaults to 1280x720, en-US, UTC, light mode, reduced motion, and blocked service workers.

actions.description: Required sequence of explicit browser actions.

storage.description: Optional initial cookies, local storage, or session storage. Defaults to empty; every supplied value and origin must be declared and within the allowed origins.

secrets.description: Optional environment-variable references for values used in actions, URLs, storage, or replay, and for redacting matching observed text. Secret values are never supplied inline.

capture.description: Optional retained artifacts and event families. Defaults to only a final sanitized URL; request screenshots, DOM, accessibility, history, storage, and event capture explicitly.

command_timeout_ms.description: CDP WebSocket handshake and per-command response deadline in milliseconds (default 20000). Omitted means 20000 and applies on the next call. deadlineExpired for a handshake or command is not the caller observation window, not the CDP discovery deadline (default 10000 ms, or discovery_timeout_ms where supported), and not the 5000 ms cleanup grace. It also bounds passive script-source collection and the inspection/source-join phase that share this deadline. Does not raise the fixed protocol, retained-event, or source byte budgets, or the cleanup grace, which have no runtime override.

detail.description: complete returns the complete analysis Evidence inline. summary retains that complete Evidence in this session and returns its inspect_analysis_view summary; inspect pages, items or facets through normalized_result.parent_evidence_id.

tools.name: observe_web_execution
tools.title: Observe Web Execution
tools.description: Instrument one selected CDP page for a finite, externally driven precise coverage window. Resets execution counters and prevents optimized execution until stopped. Returns complete nested UTF-16 ranges/counts, independently hashed script text and request initiator associations by session script ID. Does not navigate, click, evaluate selected code or close the externally owned page. Navigation ends document-scoped collection; workers and UI causality remain outside this claim. Emits an actual armed progress notification before external actions.

tools.name: inspect_web_event_listeners
tools.title: Inspect Web Event Listeners
tools.description: Inspect listeners registered directly on the first main-document CSS match in one selected CDP page. Returns event flags, native callback locations, source ownership and exact script text/digests inline. Does not dispatch events, evaluate JavaScript or invoke handlers. Delegated ancestor/framework listeners and execution history remain unknown. Releases REA's object group and transport, preserving the external page.

tools.name: inspect_web_network_capture
tools.title: Inspect Web Network Capture
tools.description: Inspect a saved local HAR 1.2, mitmproxy, Fiddler SAZ or supported aioquic qlog capture without contacting recorded URLs. Returns source-linked records, preserved producer fields, precise numbers, exposed bytes and explicit coverage/limitations; transport credentials and explicitly marked sensitive values are excluded. Use inspect_web_page for a live CDP page. Preserve capture_path exactly as supplied; it names a path on the REA host, not a path to rebase onto the client workspace. Select format; record_ordinals selects records after full decoding and also decodes recognized protobuf/gRPC bodies. Optional protobuf selects body_pointers, framing and a local FileDescriptorSet/message_type; native gRPC and gRPC-web remain distinct, ambiguous readings stay candidates and compressed payloads stay unknown. Default complete delivery is inline. detail summary retains Evidence for inspect_analysis_view kind capture (preview/complete), protobuf (bodies/frames/fields), or qlog; large text/schema values require explicit fields. Qlog supports aioquic 1.5.0 JSON qlog 0.3 and reports STREAM interval unions/endpoint loss declarations, not recovered bodies or proved network loss. SAZ preserves encoded bytes without replay/HAR conversion; encrypted archives are unsupported. Mitmproxy requires caller-supplied mitmdump 12.2.3 on Linux. Malformed or oversized captures return no partial success; browser transaction attribution and HAR text’s original bytes remain unknown.

detail.description: complete returns the complete analysis Evidence inline. summary retains that complete Evidence in this session and returns its inspect_analysis_view summary; inspect pages, items or facets through normalized_result.parent_evidence_id.

tools.name: list_electron_targets
tools.title: List Electron Targets
tools.description: List every Electron file:// page target from a selected loopback CDP endpoint. Local file paths are canonicalized after symlink resolution. Selecting an endpoint exposes every eligible target and its local path metadata.

tools.name: inspect_electron_page
tools.title: Inspect Electron Page
tools.description:
Passively inspect one Electron file page by supplying its loopback CDP endpoint and target ID. The provider rechecks that the target currently exists at that endpoint and is a local file page. Returns frames, DOM structure, resource paths, and scripts without evaluating renderer JavaScript or invoking Electron APIs. The selected endpoint exposes every local file page and its metadata to this tool.

Provide a complete input group: cdp_endpoint + target_id + [observation_ms] + [command_timeout_ms] + [include_script_sources]; cdp_endpoint + target_id + include_script_sources + [observation_ms] + [command_timeout_ms].

tools.name: analyze_javascript_application
tools.title: Analyze Javascript Application
tools.description:
Build a static application graph from a local ASAR or extracted JavaScript app without executing it. Supply input_path, e.g. {input_path:"/apps/client",source_paths:["main.js"],detail:"summary"}. Copy source_paths exactly from the inventory, not host-absolute paths inferred from input_path. Returns nodes, edges, semantic relations, integrity contradictions, coverage and unknowns. source_paths limits source analysis to exact inventoried paths without narrowing inventory or artifact identity; dependencies are not implicitly analyzed and unselected sources remain unknown. detail summary reduces delivery, retaining complete Evidence for inspect_analysis_view; it does not reduce analysis. With summary detail, view {kind:"javascript-routes",collection:"routes",offset:0,limit:64} selects static route patterns; static routes do not prove reachability or the complete route set. Integrity mismatches fail by default; record-and-continue retains untrusted observed bytes and partial coverage. analysis_timeout_ms is a per-source provider budget. A host-only timeout needs a longer client deadline, not that budget; do not repeat unchanged work or assume it stopped. If configuration cannot be edited, report the host setting (Codex: mcp_servers.<server>.tool_timeout_sec, seconds).

Advertised in reduced form by the compact input schema profile; the server still validates complete canonical inputs.

input_path.description: Absolute path to the JavaScript application on the machine running REA.

source_paths.description: Exact relevant file paths from the artifact inventory, relative to the application root, analyzed in first-request order before unselected scopes; no globs or implicit dependencies. Omit to analyze all sources.

semantic_precision.description: Per-source evaluator budgets. Omitted fields preserve defaults: primitive_candidates 256, primitive_bytes 1048576, expression_depth 256, getter_expansions 512, alias_selections 512, wrapper_visits 1000000, wrapper_depth 128. Raising these does not raise graph retention, worker memory, transfer or parent result budgets; cyclic and unsupported values remain unknown.

max_semantic_nodes.description: Maximum retained semantic nodes across the application; defaults to 100000. Worker heap and parent result admission remain enforced.

max_semantic_nodes_per_file.description: Maximum retained semantic nodes per source file; defaults to 20000, additionally bounded by max_semantic_nodes and memory/transfer limits.

max_semantic_unknowns.description: Maximum retained semantic unknown records across the application; defaults to 100000. Omitted emission occurrences are counted by family and reason.

max_semantic_unknowns_per_file.description: Maximum retained semantic unknown records per source file; defaults to 20000, additionally bounded by max_semantic_unknowns and memory/transfer limits.

max_heap_mb.description: Maximum V8 old-space heap in MiB for the isolated JavaScript source analyzer; defaults to 1024. This does not change the CLI/MCP process heap. When REA runs on Bun, which ignores V8 heap flags, Windows instead limits the analyzer's committed memory to this budget plus a 512 MiB runtime reserve; other Bun hosts enforce no limit.

analysis_timeout_ms.description: Maximum startup, analysis and transfer time per JavaScript source, in milliseconds; defaults to 300000. On timeout, return collected partial Evidence and stop the analysis.

tools.name: reconcile_javascript_runtime
tools.title: Reconcile Javascript Runtime
tools.description:
Reconcile verified static JavaScript application graphs with existing passive web/Electron CDP, passive V8 Inspector, or provider-owned active Electron Evidence. Active Electron captures contribute an explicitly partial target-only runtime record; they never invent renderer scripts, frames, workers, or execution claims. Exact captured-source digests take priority over caller-declared file/URL mappings; target, frame, script, and worker ambiguity remains explicit, and source-map authority stays separate.

Declared Evidence fields accept complete records or {"kind":"retained-evidence","evidence_id":"ev_..."}. For a complete source, use the summary's parent_evidence_id. Advertised in reduced form by the compact input schema profile; the server still validates complete canonical inputs.

tools.name: capture_electron_scenario
tools.title: Capture Electron Scenario
tools.description: Launch and exercise an owned Electron app when passive CDP/Inspector observation cannot answer the question. REA owns startup/teardown; selected click/wait, renderer reload/crash and synthetic open-url/second-instance actions change runtime behavior. Returns correlated window/WebContents/process/preload/session/navigation/shell/IPC observations without payload values, plus action targets and coverage/truncation. Actions wait for completion or cancellation; a missing click target can remain pending. External shell, navigation, permission, download, popup, updater and OS-integration effects are blocked and recorded. Cleanup failures retain observations with explicit uncertainty. Use inspect_electron_page or observe_javascript_runtime for passive observation.

tools.name: inspect_electron_fuses
tools.title: Inspect Electron Fuses
tools.description: Inspect packaged Electron fuse bytes in one local macOS app bundle, Electron Framework binary, Windows PE executable, or Linux ELF executable. Returns the artifact digest, per-slice wire version, fuse index, version-1 name, state, and raw byte, plus derived implications for Inspector flags, ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE, embedded ASAR integrity, and app.asar-only loading. A missing sentinel is unknown fuse state. Reads artifact bytes only and does not modify the selected file or open a runtime target.

tools.name: list_javascript_runtime_targets
tools.title: List Javascript Runtime Targets
tools.description: List every eligible Node/Electron V8 Inspector target from an explicit literal-loopback endpoint. Node discovery file locations that cannot be verified are preserved as unresolved reported URLs; they do not prove filesystem identity. Listing does not attach to targets.

tools.name: observe_javascript_runtime
tools.title: Observe Javascript Runtime
tools.description: Passively observe loaded-script and execution-context metadata on one loopback Node/Electron V8 Inspector target, selected by inspector_endpoint and target_id. Presence/attachability and file locations are rechecked; verified file paths stay separate from reported URLs, including distinct query/fragment identities. Parse failures are counted separately from malformed events. REA does not read source, evaluate, pause/resume or instrument execution; imports, EventEmitter activity and Electron IPC remain unknown. Use reconcile_javascript_runtime with static application Evidence. The selected endpoint exposes every target it serves to this tool.

tools.name: inspect_analysis_settings
tools.title: Inspect Analysis Settings
tools.description: Inspect REA's editable runtime admission sizes, deadlines and worker heaps, their bounds, launch values and application points. No active target is required. Filters intersect. If an error already names a setting and its bounds, update_analysis_settings can be called directly. Explicit per-call arguments override runtime defaults. Active worker values are not observed by this configuration view.

tools.name: update_analysis_settings
tools.title: Update Analysis Settings
tools.description: Atomically set or reset editable runtime defaults for new work. Changes survive target close/open but disappear on REA restart; reset restores launch configuration. Follow an error's named setting/bounds directly, then retry after work and cleanup settle; no inspection is needed when they are supplied. Does not change active work, edit files, restart providers, raise client limits or override explicit per-call arguments.

tools.name: inspect_analysis_view
tools.title: Inspect Analysis View
tools.description:
Read summaries, selected facts, or pages from completed Evidence without rerunning analysis. Use the producing tool’s retained-view handoff for compatible selectors; the examples here are not exhaustive. Copy normalized_result.parent_evidence_id from a summary into source: {kind: "retained-evidence", evidence_id: "<parent_evidence_id>"}. Other sources are {kind: "inline", evidence: <complete Evidence>} or {kind: "evidence-file", path: "<absolute JSON path>", evidence_id?: "<record ID>"}; select an ID for a multi-record bundle. For native pseudocode use {source: {kind: "retained-evidence", evidence_id: "<parent_evidence_id>"}, view: {kind: "native", facet: "pseudocode", offset: 0, limit: 128}}; procedure_pseudo_code parents support this text facet, while other native function facets require analyze_function. Common views: {kind: "summary"} has no facet; {kind: "inventory", collection: "occurrences", logical_paths: ["package.json"], offset: 0, limit: 64} selects artifact paths; {kind: "capture", detail: "preview", offset: 0, limit: 20} pages saved network records; {kind: "managed-members", collection: "methods", offset: 0, limit: 64} pages managed members. Use the producer’s named kind for other families; compact schemas may omit nested shapes, so do not invent selectors. Text offsets/limits use UTF-16 code units; row pages count the selected retained collection. Preserve parent identity, null/unavailable values, source coverage, limitations and unknowns; exhausting pages does not prove complete discovery, runtime use or absence. Smaller pages can resolve delivery limits without repeating analysis; complete parent Evidence remains available for export.

Advertised in reduced form by the compact input schema profile; the server still validates complete canonical inputs.

tools.name: inspect_api_contract
tools.title: Inspect Api Contract
tools.description:
Inspect declared APIs in local OpenAPI JSON or GraphQL SDL without a session, network requests or target execution. OpenAPI 3.0/3.1/3.2 returns inline method/path operations with source pointers; references remain unresolved. format:"graphql-sdl" returns types/fields and optional operations_path bindings, preserving aliases, fragment/spread owners and unknowns without expanding fragments or claiming full operation validation. Default summary retains Evidence; view overrides detail. For HTTP rows use view {kind:"api-contract",collection:"operations",methods:["GET"],limit:20}; GraphQL uses view {kind:"graphql-contract",collection:"references",limit:20}. inspect_analysis_view pages the same retained facts. Source declaration coverage stays separate from page exhaustion; paging does not increase parser allowances. Introspection, runtime behavior and contract comparison are outside scope.

Advertised in reduced form by the compact input schema profile; the server still validates complete canonical inputs.

path.description: Absolute path to a local API contract document

max_file_bytes.description: Maximum bytes per input document (up to 32 MiB); reply paging does not increase parser allowances

operations_path.description: Optional absolute path to one local GraphQL operation/fragment document; parsed without execution

tools.name: inspect_ntfs_journal
tools.title: Inspect Ntfs Journal
tools.description: Inspect USN V2/V3/V4 records from a local acquired NTFS journal with a caller-paired MFT from the same volume. Reads at most 64 MiB per file. Returns source-order events, explicit coverage rows, both SHA-256 identities, and nextFileOffset for another page using the same inputs. V2 MFT references include sequence numbers; opaque V3/V4 IDs remain unresolved. MFT inventory counts are inline by default; select mft_record_limit for up to 32 detailed records, including identity-checked extension attributes and explicit link coverage. V4 returns at most 16 extent samples per event with explicit omissions. History completeness remains unknown. Other journal versions and unverifiable references remain explicit. Reads only the selected acquisition files.

tools.name: inspect_playwright_trace
tools.title: Inspect Playwright Trace

tools.name: start_build_computer

Returns driver content/images and structured results, with each action logged. Points use the latest frame's pixels (take a screenshot first), or space norm on 0..norm_scale; count 2 double-clicks, drag path has 2..50 points, and keys names one W3C chord (ctrl+s is translated). Region screenshots crop the latest frame rather than recapture; use a full screenshot or wait with screenshot true first. After opening a menu/window, wait for its screenshot instead of taking the action's immediate one. type_secret reads the user-created handle file at $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/rea/build-secrets/<handle>, or ~/.config/rea/build-secrets/<handle> into a focused masked field: only the handle is recorded and no screenshot is taken, but later screenshots can expose unmasked fields. reset restores seed data through data/reset and relaunches; screenshot_error after reset does not undo it. tools.name: stop_build_capture

tools.description: Close the captured app and finish its capture. Returns checkpoints, package/sources, limitations and a draft between seed and end when both exist and no declared secret was used. later_drafts contains one draft per later end-<task name>, relative to the preceding end checkpoint. Drafts list owned-path changes, supported before/after structured values, suggested checks and optional unchanged-state guards. Notes explain missing/thin drafts and recovery: add unrecognized documents to state_paths, or make a change saved in a readable file rather than only dconf. After secret use, automatic drafting is withheld; write the tasks manually. Otherwise write each task from its draft in the user's words and pass the tasks to export_build_environment.

tools.name: export_build_environment

tools.description:
Export the stopped capture and given tasks as an agentenv app bundle, seeded at seed. Each task uses its selected end checkpoint (end by default) and its captured near-<task name> when present. The bundle's eval lists every task; verified files are copied to a new/empty host directory. Refuses publication if names or contents contain declared secrets, including UTF-16/hex/base64/URL/gzip forms; errors identify handles and files. Files under the owned paths that changed between the pre-sign-in and post-sign-in checkpoints, and those named in withhold, are withheld from the seed as sign-in or licence state: each becomes a secret setting the deploy takes from an environment variable as the file's bytes in base64, the README says how to fill it, a check may not name it, and REA keeps its bytes as the secret withheld_files names by handle, for start_build_computer's settings when witnessing; a file larger than 48 KiB cannot be withheld. With seed_sign_in, they are seeded instead, which needs a seed_sign_in consent from record_build_consent; every recorded consent ships as consent.json. A check already passing on the seed or a near miss passing every check refuses the whole export, naming the task and reason. Witness each task on a fresh computer with start_build_computer and check_build_task.

Advertised in reduced form by the compact input schema profile; the server still validates complete canonical inputs.

Witness stages run in order: seed (supply directory to begin recording) must fail a check, after_edit must pass all, near_miss must fail one, and after_reset must restore every seed result. Use the task prompt alone for the edit. Seed rejects exported task/verifier mismatches. Unreadable or truncated views are undecided, not witnessed failures; an undecidable stage is refused for retry. A failed stage or after_reset ends recording and writes witness.json plus recording segments to directory.

A solve that did not finish is run again, at most twice, and not counted. Before each solve REA stops if the largest cost so far would take the total past budget_usd; a solve's cost is known only when it ends, so the first always runs, and a solve that reports no cost stops the measure. The solver calls the model endpoint agentenv reads where REA starts: LITELLM_BASE_URL and LITELLM_API_KEY, or [model] in .agentenv/config.toml; REA holds no model client and never reads the key. It writes difficulty.json at the bundle's root, each measured task's record by name, and a Measured difficulty section in its README, and returns the record: the band, passes, finished solves (k), turns, cost, failures per check and each solve. Solves run one at a time and take minutes each; REA reports progress meanwhile.
